postTitle: Account Consolidation: Cleaning Up Financial Sprawl
topic: An old pension usually moves provider to provider, not through your own account

assumptions.notes: Jiri's €30,000 pension from a job he left (day 1 example). Direct transfer: all €30,000 stays pension money. Paid out first: many systems count it as income; at an illustrative 30% tax that is €9,000, leaving €21,000 outside any pension; some countries add an early withdrawal penalty or withhold tax from the payout. No country specific rule is used. Illustrative, not tax advice.

hookVariants.narration: An old pension that passes through your own bank account can become a taxed withdrawal.

beats.narration: Jiri has thirty thousand euros in a pension from a job he left. His current plan charges far less, so he wants to move it.
There are two ways out. Straight from one provider to the other. Or paid out to him first.
The direct route keeps every euro as pension money.
Paid out first, many systems count it as income. At an illustrative thirty percent, that is nine thousand euros in tax, and some countries add a penalty.
The usual fix is a direct transfer, which the new provider can often request.
beats.subtext: Often started by the new provider

beats.narration: And if a form offers to pay the money to you, many people pause and check for the direct route first.
beats.subtext: Pause. Check for a direct route

beats.narration: So before you move any pension, check three things. Who starts it. Where it goes. And whether anything is paid to you.

caption.instagram:
There are two ways to move an old pension. One of them can cost you thousands.

Jiri wants to move a €30,000 pension from a job he left. A direct transfer, provider to provider, keeps it pension money. Paid out to him first, many systems count it as income: at an illustrative 30%, that is €9,000 in tax, and some countries add a penalty on top.

The transfer check: in many systems the new provider starts it, the money goes provider to provider, and a form offering a payout is a signal to pause and check.
